$comment: The validation-error taxonomy, shared by all five ports. Every language's test
suite LOADS this file — TypeScript src/ErrorTaxonomy.spec.ts, Python
Hand-mirrored literals are what let these five drift apart in the first place,
so do not copy these values into a test file: read them from here.
WHY a `kind` string exists at all: catching by TYPE is not portable. TypeScript,
Python and .NET raise three distinct classes; Rust collapses them into one enum
with three variants; Go returns one struct with a Kind field. Code that has to
behave the same in more than one language cannot branch on the type, so all five
now carry the same three `kind` values and that is what it branches on.
NOT pinned here: the human-readable message. Go's is idiomatically Go
(lowercase, `file:`-prefixed) and should stay that way; forcing five languages
onto one English sentence would be parity theatre. What must match is the
machine-readable discriminant and the structured fields carried with it.

size.raisedWhen: The file exceeds the declared maximum size, or its size could not be determined.
size.$comment: actualSize is absent/None/null/-1 when the source never exposed a size.

mime.raisedWhen: The file's MIME type is not in the declared allowlist.

contentMismatch.raisedWhen: Magic-byte detection disagrees with the caller-claimed MIME type. The primary defense against MIME spoofing.

constructors.$comment: What each port names the thing that carries a given kind, so the loaders can be read side by side.
